selection_note: UPSTREAM UPGRADE BATCH: prospective Index-first S2=C hypothesis cohort, five source-disjoint included S1=A assessments on exact Index main 8ef26789403d7cf682e67dcc7985a0317a76bb00. No current third-party target implementation, issues or PRs inspected before this immutable checkpoint. All 65 rows from 13 merged cohorts and visible open Upstream PR titles/source reservations excluded. candidates.finding: Index S2=C describes tenant-shared target/action intent windows across independent incident runs. Prospectively test whether a refused or retried request is counted in a way that prematurely exhausts a target window, or a boundary-time request bypasses the shared limit; verify different targets remain independent.
candidates.blocker: No top-level source license grant or recognized GitHub SPDX license at the unchanged reviewed/current ref. First-party rate rules explicitly count planned action intents; counting a denied/retried intent is not established as a defect in the intended policy. No source-native falsifying boundary-time or cross-target test/maintainer need has been observed, and the indexed source has no checked-in Go _test.go suite. Need licensing clarity and a demonstrated supported native defect before any patch; no external write or model test.
candidates.screening_result: S2 mechanism is a tenant/tool/target action-intent count in Postgres evaluated by the configured rate rule; the assessed hypothesis remains unconfirmed, not a proved improvement. Public issue/PR inventory has no matching rate-limit change (2026-11-08).

candidates.finding: Index S2=C identifies host-wide path write locks plus per-agent read stamps across parent/child registries. Prospectively test whether a stale edit from a sibling session is refused under equivalent path aliases while independent files remain writable; falsify if existing normalization/freshness checks already cover all supported aliases.
candidates.screening_result: Current AGPL-3.0 source master@9078b2e already resolves supported file destinations to canonical paths, coordinates first-party file writes through one host-shared lock, checks recorded read freshness and refuses stale edits; explicit force=true is a supported override. No source-supported alias overwrite beyond those protections or maintainer need was independently shown. Hypothesis not substantiated; no patch and no chatbot-native test.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C describes shared-owner atomic token reservations and settlement across concurrent goal runs. Prospectively test failure/retry at reservation-to-settlement boundaries: a released or retried claim must not strand budget or double-credit an owner while another run proceeds.
candidates.observed_native_change: A separately executed, SHA-pinned GitHub Actions PostgreSQL 16 / Python 3.11 run #42493920695 reproduced both preregistered budget finalization failures on untouched first-party code: duplicate settle made remaining 1100 rather than 750 and release after settle made it 1350 rather than 750. After the reservation-id and once-only finalization patch, 8/8 first-party native tests passed (three new regressions/controls and five original budget tests), and git diff --check passed. No chatbot-executed native test, provider or agent session occurred.
candidates.limit: Benefit is confined to pinned SQL token-ledger correctness under the scripted fixture. No production/real-model throughput, third-party maintainer acceptance, Index grade change or external fork write is claimed. Archive the one-off Upstream CI runner recipe and shift any future rerun to a separately permissioned fork/host before integration.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C records failed shared-goal integration returning the exact assignee to a new revision against the latest base. Prospectively test repeated/conflicting integration completion notices and retry: only one repair should be queued, previous verified state invalidated, and unrelated changes unaffected.
candidates.blocker: Current MIT MarkChangeIntegrated(false) omits RowsAffected checks for state transitions, but enqueueSubGoalRunTx coalesces pending same-role runs in one transaction; a duplicate finished-run repair or unsupported repeated completion callback is not yet proven through the actual first-party entry point. No separate deterministic native runner baseline or maintainer need verifies the proposed repeat conflict bug. Require a supported interleaving and native failure before proposing a patch; no external write or model test.
candidates.screening_result: Source suggests a possible edge when a conflict completion is repeated after the prior assignee run finishes, but coalescing limits ordinary concurrent duplicate enqueue. This is a question, not a reproduced native flaw. Public issue/PR inventory has no matching conflict-repeat report (2026-11-08).

candidates.finding: Index S2=C credits SQLite atomic claims, attempt fencing and ancestor/descendant write-path collisions. Prospectively test whether equivalent normalized write-path declarations and stale attempts can evade shared scope exclusion while genuinely disjoint paths can still be claimed.
candidates.blocker: The Index-reviewed Python collector/coordination.py implementation is absent from current MIT main@e225cbd5; the first-party project now ships a Rust daemon/worktree design with a materially changed coordination architecture. The preregistered old SQLite write-claim alias hypothesis cannot be mapped onto the live product without a fresh Rust-native boundary review and test contract; no change or effect is asserted.
candidates.screening_result: Structural source drift from reviewed Python collector to Rust app/bin/rust tree invalidates the old code-path target; this cohort preserves the original Index question and stops rather than silently reinterpret a new Rust issue as assessment-derived.
